summary: One plan, six packages with disjoint file ownership, one Unity process at a time. Winning calls on the three conflicts: (1) DIFFICULTY: the campaign design's generator approach wins (reproducible strings, one source of truth) but its count-only multipliers lose to the fun/scope critiques; the retune is count (x1.10-1.46, introduction packets kept verbatim) + cadence (spawn gaps x1.0-0.78 by chapter, 0.85 packet overlap on pre-boss and boss levels, breathers 5/4/3 s) + HP (+2 %/level, +8 % on boss levels, +5 % on levels 1-2), generated by a checked-in scripts/carrot-waves.mjs; verified here with a scratch run: pressure (HP-weighted spawn work per stream second) rises 1.09-1.26x in chapter 0 and 1.9-2.5x on the harvest road, every boss level is its chapter's maximum, and no level's stream time grows more than 1.29x, so levels get harder, not longer. (2) BLINDNESS: the campaign design's input lock loses (two critiques: the view bypasses Command, and waiting in the dark is frustration); blindness is a simulation effect (towers outside light lose 40 % range; Prism, Sun Blossom auras and the arena's four lantern pads are the counterplay) drawn by a single camera-near-plane quad with a new Carrot/BlindOverlay shader (uGUI's UI/Default is stripped by CarrotShaderStripper, so the overlay cannot be a RawImage), plus a dimmed HTML HUD. Full dark is reserved for the Lantern Regent, Old Hollowhead's phase-3 Dusk and the Unknown Eyeball; Crown of Winter gets a white frost vignette. (3) SUPER: the super design's merge contract wins (free, drag tier-4 onto same-kind tier-4, target keeps pad, spent accumulates, cost stays 4 entries) with the fun critique's rule B: a Super equals roughly two tier-4s in trait-inclusive throughput and gains NO range, so the decision is coverage; boss-interacting traits are cut, a 4 s undo exists, and Uproot demotes a Super to tier 4 instead of destroying it. Uproot ("destroy a random plant") is one shared commit path used by Brambleback, Old Hollowhead and the Zombie (telegraph on the tower, sell-before-commit cancels, 55-60 % refund, grave knot only on the Zombie). Challenges live in the page lobby (the only main menu) as three cards on one 31-unit arena map (levels 25-27): Giant Tornado (Easy: Gust + Lift-off), Zombie (Hard: Uproot + Raise Dead), Unknown Eyeball (Insane: Blindness + Gaze); the boss arrives mid-level and the remaining waves spawn as adds (a challenge-only wave gate), so a "BossFight" card is a boss fight, not seven minutes of tower defense. Progress: two new localStorage records (cgs-carrot-super-v1, cgs-carrot-challenges-v1) with pure max/OR/min merge functions exported from the game modules; the accounts repo wiring and the level-12 clamp fix are a separate package. Sequencing: the simulation package lands the merge contract first and re-proves the 48 campaigns on the OLD waves with merging bots, then abilities, then challenge levels, then the retune; the view package starts only after the running speed-pass workflow commits; Blender work runs in parallel from day one; one ship-check package builds, measures and writes validation.md.
